subject: Urgent: Concordia - Throughput & error surge after qprofile v2 deploy
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@concordia-retail.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Concordia Platform <support@concordia-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Significant throughput drop & p50/p95 regressions after qprofile v2

Michael —

We pushed the qprofile v2 that Redwood recommended last night (00:30 PT) and immediately saw a large drop in throughput for our checkout inference path. Token throughput is down ~38% and p95 latency has jumped from ~210ms to ~540ms. We are also seeing a spike in 5xx errors (mainly 504 timeouts) across multiple pods. This is causing transactional failures in checkout and we are flagging this as Sev2.

Attached: concordia_kpi_snapshot_20280606.csv with the before/after metrics.

Can you confirm Redwood rolled anything on your side? We did the profile change on our side per the recommended qprofile vector and followed the checklist. Need an immediate rollback option or mitigation. Our VP (Dan Whitaker) is on standby.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, Concordia Retail
samira.khan@concordia-retail.com
+1 415-555-0147

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@concordia-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant throughput drop & p50/p95 regressions after qprofile v2

Samira —

Thanks for the heads-up and for the snapshot. I’m escalating to our SRE and model teams immediately (cc’d). We did not push any platform-side changes matching your timestamp; the recommend qprofile vectors were published but that should be no-op without a matching runtime rollout.

Immediate plan:
- Rishi: run a quick KV-cache warmup test and pull traces from the affected route.
- Marissa: coordinate a canary rollback with Concordia (if you want Redwood to trigger the rollback on our managed side).
- I’ll loop in our CTO if this risks broader customers.

Samira — can you confirm the exact model variant you pinned (model id + qprofile id) and whether you toggled "adaptive batching" or prefix caching? If you prefer a call, I can be on a bridge in 15.

—Michael
Michael Grant
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@concordia-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant throughput drop & p50/p95 regressions after qprofile v2

Quick findings from an initial probe:
- The qprofile-v2 binary exposes a heavier FP decode path for top-k sampling that increases per-token decode cycles; on our A100 fleet at 1k seq it's a ~30-40% CPU/GPU time increase per token in lab tests.
- We see a correlation between increased KV-cache misses and the customers who adopted the qprofile without enabling prefix caching. The Concordia traces show a cold-KV pattern on many sessions. (svc-trace attached: svc-trace-20280606.log)
- There are a handful of 504s in Redwood's edge layer timed during request bursts; upstream model instances are slow to respond under high-concurrency scenarios.

Immediate recommendations:
1) If Concordia can re-enable prefix caching and re-run the qprofile, that may recover most latency.
2) If they prefer rollback, we can help flip the deployed qprofile to v1 for their routing policy (we can do a targeted rollback for their tenant).
3) Deploy a temporary concurrency cap on the checkout route to limit bursts while we stabilize.

I’m starting a patch to the qprofile telemetry to flag high decode-time variants.

-rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@concordia-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant throughput drop & p50/p95 regressions after qprofile v2

Looping product + CS:
- Lauren: start the mutual action plan and log a formal rollback approval path (Concordia has an active enterprise contract and SLA implications).
- Soojin: coordinate billing/credit conversation if this turns into an SLA incident.

Samira — Redwood can trigger the rollback on your behalf for the affected routing policy and schedule a short maintenance window (we can revert within ~8 minutes for the tenant). Please confirm: do you want us to trigger rollback now or first try enabling prefix caching?

Also attaching a short qprofile diff for transparency (qprofile-v2-diff.txt).

-Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@concordia-retail.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dan Whitaker <d.whitaker@concordia-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Significant throughput drop & p50/p95 regressions after qprofile v2

Thanks — we do not have prefix caching enabled on the checkout route because of limited memory headroom in our edge pool. Given the immediate business impact (failed checkouts starting ~08:30 PT) and VP attention, please proceed with the tenant rollback now. We will re-open a test environment to validate prefix caching and the qprofile v2 in isolation.

Dan — looping you in. The team recommends rollback; please advise if you want a temporary capacity bump instead.

Samira

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@concordia-retail.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jun 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Rollback complete + next steps (Concordia)

Samira / Dan —

Rollback executed at 16:58 PT on 2028-06-08 for Concordia tenant routing policy. Post-rollback metrics show throughput recovered to within ~6% of baseline and p95 returned to ~230ms. We will keep the tenant on the qprofile-v1 variant while engineering finishes a safety patch and adds an opt-in guide for prefix-caching.

Next steps (owners):
- Rishi: finalize qprofile telemetry patch and ETA (target EOD 6/9).
- Lauren: prepare an incident summary and proposed SLA credit.
- Soojin + Finance: calculate pro-rated credit for affected window.
- Michael / Marissa: schedule a postmortem with Concordia leadership next week.

Attachments: post-rollback-snapshot (will be uploaded to the shared report).

Thanks for the quick coordination — we’ll follow up with the exec summary and action items.

-Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
